newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks, dollar soar after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks, dollar soar after Greenspan.

text.p: European stock markets shot to record highs on Wednesday, unleashed by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan -- the man who only last month wiped billions off share values by warning of "irrational exuberance".
The dollar also took heart from Greenspan's upbeat report on the U.S. economy on Tuesday, surging to levels against the yen and mark not seen for several years.
But gold, so often the market Cinderella, tumbled below $350 an ounce for the first time since late 1993.
For most markets, what Greenspan did not say in his testimony to the U.S. Senate on Tuesday was as important as what he did say. December's warning to investors was conspicuously absent.
"Greenspan's speech seems to have been taken very well and he didn't take the chance to knock Wall Street down to earth," said one London dealer.
Investors had feared that Greenspan would repeat his warning that world markets were overheating, which sent stock markets reeling across the globe last month.

Since then investors have regained their courage and the Dow Jones Industrial average has risen about 400 points. But this time Greenspan, the epitome of the prudent central banker, described the stock markets' performance only as breathtaking.
That was all the markets needed. The Dow closed up 40.03 points at a record 6,883.90 on Tuesday and European markets followed suit on Wednesday.
All leading European markets moved into record territory.

In London, the FTSE 100 index was up 27.8 points at 4,223.3, just off a record high set earlier in the morning. December British retail sales data were weaker than expected, but that reduced pressure for an interest rate rise, dealers said.

But Greenspan was the talk of the market. "The main point is that he seemed by no means as concerned about inflation as many people thought he would be," said the head of sales at a major British investment bank.
"Greenspan's speech suggests the chances of a near-term U.S. rate rise have receded, although you can't say they've entirely disappeared," he said.
Dealers said the FTSE was likely to pause after the morning's ascent, although it could go higher still if Wall Street continued to advance. Some said the Dow could conquer the 7,000-point level.

In Frankfurt, Wall Street and the buoyant dollar, which helps German exporters, pushed the DAX index up two percent to a record high before easing slightly. By midday it was up 52.43 at 3,029.14 on hopes of stronger earnings from German companies.
Paris told a similar story with the CAC-40 up more than 1.5 percent. At 1145 GMT it was 37 points higher at 2,447.
The dollar stormed through 1.64 marks to a 31-month high and flirted with 119 yen, a level last seen 46 months ago.
Greenspan gave the impetus, with investors noting his comment that tight U.S. labour markets had not stoked inflation. At midmorning it was at 1.6409 marks and 118.85.

Outside the U.S., an Italian interest rate cut and a weak German business climate survey on Tuesday buoyed the dollar as they pointed to lower rates in Europe, analysts said. "It's all coming together. People have set in their minds clear targets of the mid-1.60s against the mark...and 120 to 125 against the yen," said Stephen Hannah, director of research at IBJ International in London.
Gold was the odd market out, slipping below $350 an ounce for the first time since October 1993 to $349.70 from $353.65 at Tuesday's London close.
"People have been trying to force it lower this morning. It's looking very dodgy," one London-based dealer said.

Bullion has been sliding steadily since a high of $417 last February, with investors ignoring gold in favour of the surging stock markets. The decline has gathered steam this month amid fears of central bank sales.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar surged to 118.96 yen and 1.6427 marks from Tuesday's late European levels of 117.78 and 1.6240.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 29.8 points at 4,225.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 37.29 points higher at 2,447.17.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 57.71 points at 3,034.42.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fell to $349.70 from a $353.65 close in London on Tuesday. Silver slipped to $4.70 after closing Tuesday at $4.73.
